card.name: Causal link wording before drug exposure
card.fires_on: Words in adverse-event text that lead into a statement of cause or relationship, such as 'causal', 'related', 'cause' or 'relationship' just before 'to' plus a drug or treatment.

modes.label: Causal relationship to drug
modes.description: Words like causal, cause or relationship, and the 'to' after them, in postmarketing reports that cannot establish a link to the drug.
modes.example: it is not always possible to reliably estimate their frequency or establish a causal relationship<< to>> drug exposure.

modes.label: Related to illness or treatment
modes.description: The word 'related' or 'considered' before a cause such as the illness or treatment.
modes.example: in any given patient may be<< related>> to the illness being treated.

card.writes: It pushes the model to continue with correlate/correlation-type words, as in a link between two things.
card.plain: It fires on wording that asks whether an event was caused by or linked to a drug.
